title: ?creatures=pearl: the story mode with the Cutis-Maku Pearl set as its enemies, orange pearl-cored, the game's own numbers
context: Owner, 2026-10-13: "let's try regular story mode, but we replace the enemies with the Cutis-Maku-Pearl set", pointing at Jelly-Baby's handoff (docs/STALHEART-CUTIS-PEARL-HANDOFF.md, src/cutis at 3a985e1, "use PEARL_TIERS"). On the belt clash (the game's orange is its first solid core, the set's orange soft): "we can trivially edit the set to reflect orange as the first pearl-hardcoded. do so." Balance: the game's own numbers (the recommended default). Design docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-pearl-enemies-design.md; branch pearl-enemies cut from creature-enemies at e3f6ace3, local.
outcome: THE KIT (src/fx/cutis-maku, the 0a23df8 port brought up to 3a985e1): the Core keys in DEFAULT_CONFIG (membraneOpacity, coreShape, coreSize, pearlVariant, coreTint; contactDamage and health as unused data), CORE_SHAPES and coreContact; swarm.getCoreContact(i) on the shared transfer path (one transfer clock, delay uDelay/2, the absolute .014/.018 scaled by r0/0.2 as the port's other lengths) and a cored body's position() is its core; the membrane shader's uOpacity and uHardRadius (the rest shape held clear, one clock, the shell padded to twice the core round the synchronized centre); src/fx/cutis-maku/hard-core.js, the Pearl sphere only (MeshPhysicalMaterial roughness .17, clearcoat 1, the tier's coreTint), each core placed from getCoreContact and then put through what the shader does to its body after the hard block (the ground clamp, the deflate, the lift weighted as the body's own vertices, bendPoint = PLANET_BEND term for term), faded per instance by the body's life opacity. The port's own additions are kept (per-instance target/pace/hold/active/life, plantNext, shift, uPlanetR, thermal, the multicolour); a config without the Core keys (the boss lab, the creature probe) reads as the opaque soft body it was. The kit's mixed eight-tier preview (configFor/setMixed/speedFor and the per-tier geometry batches) is the lab's and is not ported. THE SET (src/content/pearl-enemies.js): PEARL_TIERS as tiers.ts derives them, orange coreShape 3 (so its membrane .32 and core .28), mapped white amoeba/phage, yellow ghost/scoutufo, blue saucer/jellyfish/gslime, orange drifter, green corona/shellback, purple barbed/prime, brown rolling, black phantom/knot; every mapped type's ENEMY_SPEC.rammable equals !cored. THE SWITCH (src/fx/creature-enemies.js `dress`, called once in src/fx/enemy-step.js spawnOne, so the sector waves, feasts, stampedes, guards and the opening's waves alike): a mapped entry keeps its type and its whole ENEMY_SPEC plus body 'pearl', so cloak, regen, erratic, jink, tactician, slow/accel on hit, heavy, boss, rammable, the radar, the contact card, the debrief and the tank's ram verdict run as for the dot cloud; a squad's stand-in keeps the dot squad's reach and draws its members as bodies round its record (a shed one deflates); a record coming up more than 1.2 rad round the planet from the heart (the canyon's swarm, where the bodies' plane is singular) keeps its dot cloud. THE BODIES (src/fx/creature-pearl.js on the src/fx/creature-bodies.js seam): one swarm per tier, slots freed only by death (identity never shifts), r0 = size x 5.6 m (the knot x 1.5) as per-instance scale over the tier's smallest type, times the record's hit-point shrink; the seam now also passes the stand-in's opacity (the emergence and the phantom's cloak fade membrane, inner core and pearl), the shrink, the squad's members and the record's speed. FOLLOWING (src/domain/pearl-bodies.js, PEARL_FOLLOW): the hop paced so one hop's forward reach covers 0.8 of the record's walk a cycle (the stalks' forward share 1 / 0.35 / 0.75 for one / two / three), floor 0.1; the hunt point 0.6 of its own hop ahead (CREATURE_FOLLOW's 1.8 s put fast bodies 11 radii ahead); the leash at least 1.5 s of the record's walk; separation 0.5 (the kit's 2 fought the records' own clumps).
alternatives: rewrite the queue at sector-run's creatures hook only (the task's suggestion): it misses the expedition guards, the opening's construction waves and every other storyApi.spawn; dressing at spawnOne covers every path with one call
one swarm per game type: fifteen pools and twice the draw calls; one per Pearl tier with per-instance scale keeps the handoff's stable per-tier pool
the set's own hop cadence and CREATURE_FOLLOW unchanged: offline, every type was re-placed hundreds of times a minute (records walk 8-23 m/s, the bodies are 2-7 m)
a squad as one larger body: loses the members being shed; five bodies round the record show it
port the dodecahedron and pyramid cores too: the game uses the Pearl set only (the spec)
the set's prototype health and contact damage: the owner kept the game's numbers
evidence: node test/cutis-maku-cores.mjs (the Core keys; the JS core on the membrane shader's own centre, the hard block pinned verbatim and transcribed, worst 1e-5 of the shell over 12 s of hops at r0 0.2-6.7 m, inside the padded shell at every sampled phase of all five stages; bendPoint = PLANET_BEND; the drawn core deflated, sunk and faded with its body; a config without the Core keys stays uOpacity 1 / uHardRadius 0); node test/pearl-enemies.mjs (eight tiers, orange cored, tiers.ts's derived values; every type of the wave programme mapped, each one's rammable = !cored, r0 = size x 5.6 with the knot x 1.5, the spec kept whole; pace, lead, leash, squad spots, arc; the core inside its padded shell and bent as the shell for every cored tier at its types' sizes; the family: per-type size in one swarm, following, the cloak, the shrink, stable slots reused only after a death, the squad shedding, the deflate; dress: type and spec kept, the far side and unmapped types left alone, off without the switch); the existing cutis-maku-swarm, boss-cutis-scenario and creature tests unchanged. npm test 242 programs, npm run check, npm run build (after npm ci in the worktree), npm run architecture (td-tab.js 6141 of 6400, untouched)

scripts/browser-lock.sh node scripts/browser-test.mjs --pearl-story: PASS. Sector 2's own waves came up dressed (amoeba 60, ghost 28, phage 16, barbed 3; 107 dressed, 0 far, 0 mapped records as dot clouds); with the harness's spawnFodder of nine types every tier's swarm up (white 97, yellow 51, blue 3, orange 3, green 3, purple 6, brown 3, black 4) and every cored tier's pearls drawn; a rolling mine hit once shrank and, killed, deflated (brown deaths 1); a phantom's body opacity followed its cloak (0.095-0.197 against the stand-in's 0.09-0.187); 0 page errors. The first run re-placed the white tier 160 times for 97 bodies (yellow 2 for 51): the kit's separation 2 fought the records' own clumps; offline, sixty amoebas on a clump of records: separation 2 1.9 re-placements a body-minute and 5.3 radii off, 0.5 0.03 and 2.9; at 0.5 the rerun re-placed white 30 times
--creature-probe (the eight Cutis and Reed tiers) and --boss-cutis: all PASS on this branch, first run

--sector-probe SECTOR=4 PROBE_S=50 with and without &creatures=pearl: the same timeline (alive 569 at 14 s ... 592-593 at 40 s, lost at 42 s, lost-shown at 44 s): the switch changes the picture, not the fight

offline follow simulation through src/fx/creature-pearl.js (ten bodies a type, a minute on a wandering record at its type's speed x the sector's 1.5, the erratic bursts in): one- and three-stalk tiers 1.5-2.6 radii from their records on average, never re-placed; the two-stalk tiers 2.8-5 radii, 0.1-2.4 re-placements a body-minute; the saucer (23 m/s in a 2 m body) worst at ~11 radii and 3.4

not verified: the canyon's swarm keeping its dot clouds (the 1.2 rad rule is node-tested, no browser run of the canyon sector); a squad of Pearl bodies in the browser (sector 2 sends none; node-tested); the headed M4 frame time over a real sector (owed, as the spec says); headless frame times mean nothing
